title: Morning at the Wet Market
text:
My grandmother refuses to buy vegetables anywhere but the wet market, and she refuses to go after eight o'clock. The good things, she says, are gone by then.
The floor is always slightly wet, which is how the place earned its name. Fish lie on beds of crushed ice, their eyes bright as glass. Fans turn slowly overhead. Everywhere there is the sound of bargaining, half in dialect and half in English, conducted with great seriousness by people who have known each other for thirty years.
Grandmother knows every stall holder by name, and every stall holder knows exactly how she likes her fish cleaned. It takes twice as long as the supermarket. She says that is precisely the point.
